whenToUse: News people should know even outside the app, such as a shipment leaving or a booking time.
People chose the topics they want to receive.
Timing matters and email would be too late.
whenNotToUse: You'd ask for permission as soon as the page opens (most people refuse, and you can't ask again).
The news isn't wanted, such as ads or nudges to come back.
It's feedback while people are looking at the app (use a toast or notification center).

alternatives.name: Notification Center
alternatives.reason: Keeping news inside the app to show on the next visit.

alternatives.name: Toast
alternatives.reason: Telling people who are looking at the screen right now.

accessibility: Request permission only when people press a button that explains what they'll receive.
If permission is denied or the browser doesn't support it, a role="status" message gives the reason and the fix.
The on-screen preview is a decorative imitation of a real notification, so it's aria-hidden.
System notifications follow the operating system's accessibility settings (voice, vibration, do not disturb).
